items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: And Jim LaRocca is related to Nick LaRocca in some way. I don't know whether he's son or uncle, one or the other. He's son.

ctx.x: And now they have different bands. Now there's three five piece bands there now.

You have Tony Mitchell. Tony Mitchell and the Famous Door Five. And you have Thomas Jefferson and his Creole Jazz Band. And at night you have, well, in the midst of a change right now, Jim LaRocca's going in at night now. Tommy Yedda was there at night, but he left. And Jim LaRocca is related to Nick LaRocca in some way. I don't know whether he's son or uncle, one or the other. He's son. And what about Jimmy Isle? Where is he? Jimmy Isle moved down to the Maison Bourbon. He has the early shift there. They work…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: Morez, Sr., Bob Coquille, string bass who actually played in New Orleans, and Johnny Stein who lives in New York.

ctx.x: Their champion was a colored man. Let's say a colored man has his rightful place in any music. Why not the white man to eulogize another man that hasn't created anything because of his color? That must be his music. But although Elvin Presley went on to hikes while the other guy stayed there, if you listen to his style, he couldn't have been original because he changed four or five different times. First his rhythm was based on the tango. Then he changed it to something else. Elvin Presley stuck to one style and…

This is a letter. Headed Paris, December 16, 1956. Dear Mr. LaRocca, The very long trip I have done through the world is at its end. I am just arrived from Melbourne this morning with a great regret not to have been in New Orleans for meeting you. But fate is blind and can offer me a very next opportunity to go to the States for another film. I suppose you have well received my letter dated November the 11th that I have sent you from Calcutta. If you don't, I will mail you a copy. The 1956 Olympic Games were very…

Cafe what wonderful music the Tom Brown Band had, and he wired us an offer to play at his place. The price was right, I'm sorry, to play at his place, period. The price was right and we accepted the job, period. That is how this dance team helped give our music a start, period. They were the first ones to tell Chicago about the Browns Dixieland Band, period.
